body:
Below are five ways of choosing. For each, say whether the choice model can express it, and whether it fits the rational man paradigm:

  1. a

    the agent picks whatever makes some other person suffer most;

  2. b

    the agent has his two children rank the options, then takes the option whose average rank is lowest;

  3. c

    the agent fixes an ideal point and, using a distance function, takes the option nearest to it;

  4. d

    the agent takes the option that occurs most frequently in the choice set;

  5. e

    the agent fixes an ordering of X and always takes the median element.

Answer

(a) Rational: the choice function is rationalized by ≿ itself, whatever it ranks. (b) Not rational in general: a counterexample is machine-checked. (c) Rational, for any real-valued “distance”. (d) Outside the set-based model; choice from lists is taken up in Problem 6. (e) Not rational in general: the median of a menu can violate condition α.
